transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I really hope I'm not wasting your time with this. It's... well, it's a little embarrassing to talk about, honestly, because I'm a barber. 

But I've been having this issue where I'm just... I've gotten to the point where I'll do almost anything to avoid using a straight razor at work. I know how ridiculous that sounds, right? A barber who can't use a razor? But I've been, um, making up excuses. Like, I'll try to switch clients with the other guys, or I'll even hide the tool in my drawer and tell the customer that my blades are missing. 

It's just that if I get cornered and absolutely can't get out of doing a shave... I just end up shaking through the whole thing. I try really hard to hide it from the clients because I want to be professional, but it's getting so difficult. Does that... does that make sense? I just really want to fix this so I can do a good job.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Um, no, I don't think so. I hope I'm giving you the right answer here, but I wouldn't really say it's a sudden, intense thing like that. Like an attack out of nowhere? No, I haven't had that. 

It's really just... just the nerves and the shaking when I'm actually holding the razor or know I have to use it. It doesn't suddenly peak in a few minutes or anything dramatic like that. I don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is, you know? It's just me getting really tense. I hope I'm explaining that okay?
Is your anxiety about using the straight razor limited to when you're at work, or does it happen in other situations as well?

Um, well, it's pretty much just at work, I think. I mean, I don't really have a reason to use a straight razor anywhere else, you know? At home, I just use a regular electric trimmer for myself. 

So, yeah, it's really just when I'm at the shop and I have to do a hot towel shave or line someone up with the straight blade. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture. It's really not this huge, overwhelming thing that ruins my whole life or anything... it's just this one specific tool at work that I'm having a little trouble with right now. Is that... is that helpful?
Is your anxiety about using the straight razor affecting any parts of your life outside of being a barber?

Um, outside of being a barber? No, not really. Like I said, I don't want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart, because it's not. I'm doing okay, mostly. 

But, um... at work, it is causing a few, well, hiccups, I guess you could say. I mean, I've lost out on some tips, which isn't great. And a couple of my regular clients have... well, they've mentioned it, or complained a little, because I keep trying to pass them off to the other guys when they ask for a shave. I just tell them the other guys are better at it, you know? 

And, um, I did actually back out of this local barber battle recently. It was a competition thing, and they required razor detailing, so I just... I made up an excuse not to go. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad barber or anything. I really do care about my job. I'm just trying to manage this the best I can. Does that answer your question okay?
Is your anxiety about using the straight razor more about the possibility of making a mistake in front of clients, or is it more about the physical act of using the razor itself?

Um, I think... well, it's not really about looking bad or making a mistake in front of people. I mean, I care about my clients and I want them to be happy, obviously! But it's... it's the razor itself. 

I hope I don't sound completely incompetent saying this, because I promise I'm really good at my job. I can use clippers and shears all day long, no problem at all. And I know the straight razor is just a tool, right? I trained with it for hours in barber school, I know exactly how to hold it. 

But... um... when it's just sitting there open at my station, it just feels like... like I'm about to hurt somebody, or cut myself really badly. I know that sounds terrible, and I would *never* actually do that. I'm very careful! It's just this feeling I get about the blade itself when it's open. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right, I just don't want you to think I'm a danger to anyone or anything like that.
Is your anxiety about the razor related to the sharpness of the blade or something else about it?

Um, I don't really know, to be honest. I mean, obviously, it's sharp, and that's the whole point of it, right? You need it to be sharp to get a clean shave. So I don't think it's just the sharpness, because scissors are sharp too, and I use those all the time without any issue. 

I guess I've never really thought about exactly *what* it is about the razor that bothers me. It's just... I don't know, maybe the way it looks when it's open? Or just the idea of it? I'm not entirely sure. I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a better answer. I hope that's okay? I just haven't really broken it down like that before.
Is there something specific about the way the straight razor looks or feels when it's open that contributes to your anxiety?

Um, I'm really not sure, to be honest. I mean, I've tried to figure it out, because I want to get past this, you know? I want to be the best barber I can be. 

But when it's open, it's just... I don't know, it's just a feeling I get. There's not really a specific thing about how it looks or feels in my hand that I can point to. It's just the whole... situation with it being open, I guess. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not very helpful for you to figure out what's wrong with me. I really wish I could give you a clearer answer on that. Is it okay that I don't really know exactly what part of it is causing the problem? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you think you would feel anxious about using a straight razor if you were using it on yourself, rather than on a client?

Um, well... I actually don't know, because I've never tried to use one on myself. I always use a safety razor at home. 

I mean, I imagine I'd still be pretty nervous if I tried it on my own neck, just because of how I feel when it's open at the shop. But I really couldn't say for sure if it would be exactly the same feeling or not. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you very good answers today! I hope it's not frustrating that I haven't tested it on myself. I just try to avoid it as much as I can, you know? Does that make sense, why I wouldn't have tried it at home?
Would you feel anxious about using a straight razor if you were in a different profession and had to use it for a task unrelated to shaving?

Um, gosh, that's a really interesting question. I... I've never really thought about using it for anything else. 

I mean, I guess if I had to use it to, like, cut cardboard or something? I honestly don't know if I'd still get that same awful feeling. I want to say maybe it wouldn't be as bad, since it's not near someone's skin, but... just thinking about having the blade open in my hand, I feel like my heart would still start racing. 

But I'm really just guessing here, since I've only ever held one at the barbershop. I hope it's alright that I don't have a solid yes or no for that? I feel like I'm being so unhelpful with all these "I don't knows," and I really want to give you the right information so you can help me. Am I doing okay with these answers?
Would your anxiety about using a straight razor be less if you were using it in a non-work setting, like at home, for a purpose unrelated to barbering?

Um... well, that's another one I'm just not entirely sure about. I don't actually keep any straight razors at my house, to be honest. I leave all my gear at the shop because... well, I just prefer not to have them around my apartment at all. So I've never really had the chance to try using one for, like, opening a package or doing a craft or something at home. 

I'd like to think maybe I'd be a little calmer since there's no pressure from work or clients, but... just picturing having the open blade in my living room, I think I'd still get that same panicked feeling. 

I am so sorry, I feel like I'm just giving you the exact same 'I don't know' answer again. Is it okay that I just avoid them completely outside of the shop? I really hope I'm not making your job harder by not having tried these things out. Are these answers still helpful for you?
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were cutting something with a straight razor that wasn't related to shaving, like cutting a rope or a piece of fabric?

Um, gosh, that's... that's kind of similar to the cardboard thing, I guess. I... I really don't know for sure, because I've never tried cutting rope or fabric with one. We just don't really have a reason to do that at the shop, and like I said, I don't keep them at home.

I want to say that maybe it wouldn't be quite as terrifying if it was just a piece of cloth? But honestly... just the thought of holding the open blade, feeling the weight of it, knowing how incredibly sharp it is... I'm pretty sure my hands would still start sweating and I'd get that awful tightness in my chest. 

I feel terrible, I'm just giving you the exact same non-answer over and over again. I'm really trying to think about these scenarios for you, I promise. It's just so hard to know for sure when I've spent so much energy just trying to stay away from them whenever I don't absolutely have to use them. Am I being too difficult? I really want to be a good patient and give you what you need to figure this out.
Do you think you would feel anxious if you were using a different sharp object, like scissors or a craft knife, to cut something?

Um, no, actually! Scissors and clippers and all that... I'm totally fine with those. I use them all day long without even thinking about it. It's... it's just the straight razor. 

I know it sounds so silly, because it's just a tool, right? Like, I went to school for this, I trained with it, I know how to use it safely. But... I don't know, when it's just sitting there open at my station, it's like my brain just short-circuits. I get this overwhelming feeling that I'm going to slip and hurt somebody, or cut myself really badly. 

It's embarrassing, honestly, being a barber who's afraid of a razor. I really hope you don't think I'm completely incompetent at my job. I'm actually really good with the clippers! Is it... is it normal to just have a problem with this one specific thing, even when everything else is fine? I really want to make sure I'm explaining this right for you.
Do you think your anxiety about straight razors would be present if you were not a barber?

Um... gosh, that's an interesting question. I... I honestly don't know for sure. I mean, if I wasn't a barber, I probably wouldn't ever have a reason to even be near a straight razor, right? So I guess I wouldn't have the chance to feel anxious about them. 

But... if you mean, like, if I just encountered one randomly in another life? I... I think I probably still would be scared of it. It's just the object itself, the way it looks and feels, that really sets me off. 

I hope that makes sense? I know I'm probably not giving you very concrete answers about all these hypothetical situations. I'm really trying my best to picture them for you. Is it okay that I'm not totally sure about that one either? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you think you would have developed this anxiety about straight razors if you had chosen a different career?

Um... wow, that's... that's really similar to what you just asked, isn't it? I'm sorry, I hope I didn't confuse you with my last answer! 

I... I guess I really don't know if I would have developed it if I did something else for a living. Like I said, I probably wouldn't even come across them if I worked in an office or something. But... I mean, the fear feels so strong, so attached to just the razor itself, that I feel like it would still happen if I ever had to hold one, no matter what my job was. 

But really, I'm just guessing. I don't want to tell you the wrong thing. Am I... am I supposed to know the answer to that? I'm sorry, I know I'm not being very helpful with these "what if" questions. I'm really trying, I promise. Is there... is there a right answer you're looking for here? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Would your anxiety about straight razors be present if someone else was holding it, but you were still in the barbershop?

Um... oh, wow, yeah. Definitely. It doesn't even have to be me holding it. 

I know that sounds... I mean, I hope that doesn't make me sound completely crazy. But honestly, the second I hear a client ask one of the other guys for a razor shave, or... or even if I just catch out of the corner of my eye that a blade is flipped open at the next station... it's like my whole body just reacts. My chest gets all tight, my hands get super sweaty, and... and it's like my body just wants to back away before I can even process what's happening. 

I try to hide it, you know? I don't want the other barbers to see me freaking out over something they do ten times a day. I just kind of step back and try to look busy with something else. Is that... is that an okay way to handle it? I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm, like, a danger to be around or anything. I just get so tense when they're out, no matter who has them. Does that make sense?
Would you feel anxious if you saw a straight razor in a museum or a store, where it's not being used for shaving?

Um... gosh, you know, I haven't really thought about that. I don't think I've ever actually seen one in a museum or anything like that. 

I guess... I mean, if it was locked in a glass case or something, maybe it wouldn't be quite as bad? Because I'd know no one could touch it or accidentally drop it. But... I think just seeing the shape of the blade would still make me feel a little bit uneasy. My heart might still race a bit, just looking at it. 

I don't know for sure, though, since it hasn't happened. I hope that's an okay answer? I feel like I'm giving you a lot of "maybes" today, and I really want to be helpful. Is it alright that I'm just guessing on some of these?
Would you feel anxious if you saw a straight razor in a context completely unrelated to barbering or shaving, such as in a historical reenactment or a theatrical performance?

Um... gosh, I'm sorry, I really don't know. I haven't been to a play or a reenactment or anything like that in a really long time. 

I guess... if I knew for sure it was just a fake prop, like made of plastic or rubber, I'd like to think I'd be completely fine. I definitely don't want to sound like I can't even go to a normal theater without panicking, you know? But... if I knew it was a real blade they were holding on stage, even if they weren't shaving with it... yeah, I'd probably still get pretty tense. I'd probably be watching it the whole time, just waiting for it to be put away. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I keep letting you down with these hypothetical questions since I just haven't been in those situations. Is it okay that I don't have a definite yes or no for this one? I just feel bad that I can't give you a solid answer. Am I still giving you what you need to figure this out? I really don't want to make your job harder.
Would your anxiety about straight razors be less intense if you were to handle one in a completely safe and controlled environment, such as a therapist's office?

Um... wow, that's... that's a tough one to think about. I mean, being in a safe place like this, with someone like you who knows what they're doing... I'd really like to say yes. I'd like to think I could be brave enough to handle it if I knew I was totally safe. 

But... honestly? Just the thought of holding one right now, even here... my hands are getting a little sweaty just picturing it. I think I would still be pretty terrified. I don't think I could even bring myself to touch the handle, let alone hold it. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for. I really wish I could say I'd be fine in a controlled environment. Does that make me seem completely unreasonable? I just want to be totally honest with you, even if it makes me look a little... weak. Is it normal to still be that scared even when you know you're safe?
Would your anxiety about straight razors be present if you were to encounter one in a completely unrelated context to your work as a barber, such as at a friend's house or in a non-work setting?

Um... yeah, I think it definitely would still be there, even if I wasn't at work. 

It's... it's kind of embarrassing to admit, honestly, especially since I'm a barber. I know it's just a tool. I was trained with it, you know? I can use clippers and scissors all day long without a second thought. But... if I saw a straight razor sitting open, even if it was just on a counter at a friend's house... it's like my brain just jumps to the worst-case scenario. 

When it's sitting open at my station at work, it feels like... like I'm about to hurt somebody, or like I might slip and cut myself really badly. And I think I'd feel that exact same dread no matter where it was. 

I'm really sorry, I know that sounds terrible for someone in my profession. I really don't want you to think I'm incompetent at my job. I'm usually very good at what I do, I promise. Does that make sense, though? That it feels dangerous to me even though I know it's just a tool? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Would your anxiety about straight razors be present if you were to use one in a setting that is identical to your workplace, but you were not being paid or considered to be 'on the job'?

Um... gosh, yeah, I think... I think the panic would still be exactly the same. 

Even if I wasn't officially on the clock or getting paid, it's... it's still me holding that blade, you know? If I had to actually use one, even just doing a favor for a friend after hours or practicing... I'd still be absolutely terrified of it slipping or doing some kind of horrible damage. The money or the job title part doesn't really seem to change how my chest gets all tight just thinking about it.

I know that probably sounds so silly. I really, really wish I could tell you that taking the pressure of work away would fix it. I'd love to just be normal about it and say I'd be fine. I hope it's okay that I'm admitting this... I don't want you to think I'm just making excuses or that I'm completely useless as a barber. I really do try my best with all my other tools. 

Does that help answer your question? I'm sorry if I feel like a broken record with all these scenarios, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can figure this out. Am I doing okay?
